official_FS90MG: datasheets/FS90MG.pdf p.5, edition A/0, 2021-04-30, all ±0.1 mm

servos.head_pan: FS90MG in yaw_collar, software ±42°, hard stop ±47°
servos.head_tilt: FS90MG on neck_turret, axis along x through y=6, z=119; software ±10°, first contact +12.0° (nod down) / -15.5° (look up)

hug.mechanism: Mirumi-style passive hug: each arm turns on a vertical M3 hip pin; a music-wire torsion spring in the knuckle closes it onto a printed rest stop; opened by hand to a 40° printed stop; zero power to hold

spring.part: music-wire torsion spring, 0.048 in (1.22 mm) wire, 3/8 in (9.5 mm) OD, 90° legs (trim to ~6 mm); catalogue 3HPG6 (LH) / 3HPD1 (RH)

hug.arm_angle_convention: 0 = closed on the rest stop, + = open; rotation about z through each hip (x=±49.95, y=−16.19)
hug.groove: R8 channel down the belly, floor y = −30 − 0.25(z − 30) (leans 14°), z 12–62, 2.4 mm liner

grip.object: round Ø10.0 lying in the groove (leans 14°)
round Ø12.5 lying in the groove (leans 14°)
round Ø15.0 lying in the groove (leans 14°)
flat strap 25 x 2.5 resting on the belly across the groove

open.note: Ø15 rod slid in along the groove normal from 60 mm out to the groove floor with both arms on the open stop; the last 3 steps are the clamp zone.

hug.assumption: Spring rate from the catalogue (2.679 lbf·in at 90°), linear; no friction in the hinge; force = torque / perpendicular lever from the hinge axis to the pad contact line. TPU pads assumed rigid for the angle (real pads add ~1 mm of squash). Not measured.

hanging_verdict: On paper it holds: the springs give 5.2 N total at the paws, more than the 3.9 N (4.5 N with a battery) needed to carry the pitch moment, and the friction safety factor is about 3.5 (3.3 with a battery). The body hangs leaning back 14° along the groove; com_x ≈ 0, so it does not roll sideways. Untested; real strap friction and fur squash will decide it.

servo_power.note: Arms are passive and draw nothing; hugging costs no power. Budget the 5 V servo rail for ≥1.6 A peak.
